class_sheet: Bell eats counter (results: Chaotic; level-0 note: chaotic bell eats counter)
class_guess: Bell eats counter: signed base-4 counter on 3-cell digits, bitten by a growing bell (W4-2 architecture)
summary: Each round adds 1 to a base-4 counter and walks a defect 1 block left; then the bell bites the counter's low end.
mechanism: Round start K(w,b,c) = 0^inf w 0 E> 101 (001)^b 0001 (001)^c 0^inf; w = 3-cell digits x0y worth 2x-y (001=-1, 000=0, 101=1, 100=2). Round (b>=3): K(w,b,c) -> K(w+1,b-1,c+1) in 12b+22+14t(+4) steps, exact, 300/300.

Eat (b=2): 1-7 sub-rounds over the bell; the boundary moves left d = 3j+2 cells (pure bite for d>=5), b' = c+1..c+5, so L grows ~1-3 per eat and L ~ step^(1/3). The 2-cell alignment shift leaves dirty digits 010/011, which later carries clean.

Halting routes exist (round on ...1 110; eat on a 111 top, fed by eats on 011 tops), but to 3e10 steps (1,597 eats) no pre-eat counter has a 011/111 top: avoidance looks structural, as in W4-2. No closed form for the eat yet.

rules.name: ROUND (clean counter)
rules.steps: 12b+22+14t (+4 if the digit that absorbs the carry is 000 or blank)
rules.cases: b >= 3; w over the clean digits 001,000,101,100 (values -1,0,1,2); w+1 = +1 in base 4 with digits {-1,0,1,2}; t = number of trailing 100 digits

rules.name: ROUND step count
rules.cases: t = carry length; fitted on 40 random instances, k <= 6 digits, b <= 40

rules.name: ROUND (dirty counter)
rules.cases: exhaustive: every 1-3 digit word over {001,000,101,100,011,010} with a dirty digit, 40-70 rounds each: no halt, never another code, always clean again after the carry passes (no closed form for w' yet)

rules.name: EAT shape
rules.to: K(w', c+delta, c'), delta in 1..5, c' in 0..6
rules.cases: random clean words (1-7 digits, 1500) and 30%-dirty words (1500), c = 20..120: no halt, always returns to K-form; w' has no closed form yet

rules.name: EAT bite (real run)
rules.cases: d >= 5: the cells left of the new boundary are unchanged (pure bite); d = 2: 1-8 cells near the new boundary rewritten (a carry/borrow); 496 eats to 1e9 (4 early eats with d = 0)

rules.name: HALT route A
rules.cases: 001110, 101110, 011110, 111110 (all 2-digit words with low block 110 and a 1 left of it)

rules.name: HALT route B
rules.cases: e.g. 111001011, 111000001, 111000101 for c = 30, 31, 32; top-011 words (14 of 3 digits) instead leave a 110/111 top after the eat

template.diff: different table (not a near neighbour); same architecture as our W4-2 kill (BECv5 TM1/TM2 plus an invariant)
template.note: BECv5/W4-2: K(w,n,m) = w <A 1 (10)^(1+n) 0 (10)^m, bounce n-1, m+1, w -> phi(w) (binary +1); overflow at n = 0 bites q+1 trailing cells, parity of q decides safety. Here: the same bounce rule with a signed base-4 counter on 3-cell digits, the overflow is a multi-sub-round eat at b = 2 that bites d = 3j+2 cells and re-aligns the digits, and halting needs a dirty top digit (011/111) under a deep bite. RIncs/LIncs-style lemmas carry over in shape; the eat and the dirty-digit tracking are new.

strategy: 1) Derive the eat exactly: the left E-run through the low digits and the B sub-rounds over the bell, giving d = 3j+2 and w' from w's low digits. 2) Abstract simulator on (w,b,c), checked against direct simulation. 3) Look for a W4-2-style invariant: dirty high digits are cleaned by carries before a bite deep enough to reach them.
risks: The path to the halting cycle (1.82e18 steps) is not directly simulated; it rests on the cycle model (eat bell-size independence, round b-independence, clean-increment arithmetic), checked on all 611,577 eats, ~2.0M oracle rounds, 1,572 direct cycles and 22,905 independently recomputed cycles.
A Rocq certificate needs parametric eat/round lemmas for this table and a checked replay of 611,577 cycles (C2-552 style); effort is large but mechanical.
No exact total step count yet (dominant term 1.8168e18).
